text: When the chapter is read beside the earlier promise, the distance between the two is diminished. Isaac is again before us as the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; and the promise, instead of remaining only promise, is made the very matter of the test. On the single Hebrew word _hineni_, "here I am," much of the scene depends. Abraham speaks it three times, to God, to Isaac, and to the angel; and in each utterance its import is changed, and its cost increased. Presence to God and to others is here inseparable from loss, as Abraham answers God, Isaac, and the angel.
